answer: Resist sybils by treating each identity as a vertex in a trust graph, not a free account. A new vertex is admitted only when several established, distant peers vouch for it, with each voucher's endorsements capped per round. A sybil farm faces a graph problem: its fake vertices cluster together, joined to the honest region by few attack edges, so random-walk audits rarely cross it and the cluster stands out. Honest standing grows like basalt on a mesa, from many supports, not one pillar. Attackers must build real relationships, not mint accounts; newcomers in sparse regions may wait longer.
